# Vistaro

> Product demos as code, built for your coding agent. You describe a demo in one sentence; an agent (Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity) writes two text files in your repo — a screen (`index.html`) and a timeline (`anim.config.json`) — and the Vistaro CLI compiles them into demo videos, step-by-step help guides, marketing reels, interactive tours and every locale. Free and open source (ISC). Runs locally and headless with no API key and no account; ffmpeg is bundled and Chromium comes via Playwright. Requires Node.js 20.6+.

## How it works

- The agent writes two files: a faithful HTML mockup of the UI and a JSON timeline of steps (click, type, camera, highlight, scroll, animate, and more).
- The CLI validates the timeline against the real page (`check`), previews frames (`preview`), then compiles outputs (`export`, `guide`, `tour`, `build`, `localize`).
- Because the demo is source, it diffs pixel-by-pixel in CI and regenerates when the UI changes, instead of rotting like a screen recording.
- No LLM is required for the pipeline itself; only the optional `extract` (screenshot→HTML) and `animate` (prompt→timeline) commands use a model, and agents skip them by writing the timeline directly.

## Outputs from one timeline

- Demo videos (MP4) with subtitles (.vtt), chapters and optional narration.
- Step-by-step help guide sites (guide.json / guide.md / guide.html + frames).
- Marketing reels: short, silent, looping product clips for desktop and phone (portrait), as MP4/WebM/poster/GIF or an embeddable page.
- Interactive tours: a scenario rail plus a canvas that plays each scenario step by step; embeddable via an `<anim-tour>` custom element.
- Localization: the same artifacts in every language from one shared choreography.

## Getting started

- Install in your project: `npm install --save-dev vistaro`, then `npx playwright install chromium` (the browser it records with, about 150 MB; npm 12 and pnpm skip install scripts, so this line is required). ffmpeg is bundled; no API key needed.
- If an agent drives it, paste one instruction: "Install vistaro as a dev dependency (npm install --save-dev vistaro, then npx playwright install chromium), read node_modules/vistaro/AGENTS.md, and create a product demo of my site." The agent reads its manual (AGENTS.md) and runs everything locally.
- To drive it yourself: `npx vistaro init-config demo`, then `check`, `preview`, `export`. From a clone of the repository, the same commands are `npx tsx cli.ts …`.
